claims.text: jev-router launches the native coding CLIs through a local proxy and selects a model tier for each new user turn.

evidence.quote:
Automatic per-turn model routing for Claude Code and OpenAI Codex. Jev sends simple work to
the fast tier and difficult work to the strong tier, while preserving each CLI's native
interface, tools, sessions, permissions, and authentication.

| Command | Interface | Authentication | Routing decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `jev-claude` | Claude Code | Existing `claude login` | Status line |
| `jev-codex` | OpenAI Codex | Existing `codex login` | Commentary line |

Both commands launch the real upstream CLI. Jev only chooses the model for a fresh user turn.

claims.text: One Jev call recommends a tier; local policy honors explicit model requests, confidence gates and conversation size before routing.
Install jev-router with npm, configure JEV_API_KEY, and launch jev-claude or jev-codex with an installed, authenticated upstream CLI.

evidence.quote:
Requires Node.js 20.12+ and at least one supported CLI:
[Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup) or
[OpenAI Codex](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli).

### 1. npm package

```bash
npm install -g jev-router
echo "JEV_API_KEY=..." > ~/.jev-router.env
```

Get a key from [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai). Then launch either interface from any
repository:

```bash
jev-claude
jev-codex
```

claims.text: Tool continuations keep their initial tier; Jev failure keeps the current model. Temporary explanation files contain the prompt and exact routing exchange.

evidence.quote:
Claude filenames use Claude Code's session UUID. Codex filenames use
`codex-<jev-codex-process-id>.json`. These temporary files contain prompt text and Jev's exact
request and response, so they are readable only by you (the directory is created with mode 700 and each
file with 600). Files not updated for 7 days are deleted automatically, and the operating system
may also remove them during normal temporary-file cleanup.

it.title: jev-router — Modello per turno Claude Code/Codex
it.h1: jev-router — Scelta del modello per turno in Claude Code e Codex
it.description: jev-router: Jev suggerisce un livello per ogni nuovo turno Claude Code o Codex, con regole locali di confidenza e sessioni CLI native.
it.summary: jev-router avvia le CLI originali tramite un proxy locale e sceglie un livello di modello per ogni nuovo turno utente. Installa con npm, configura JEV_API_KEY e avvia jev-claude o jev-codex con la CLI originale installata e autenticata.

sections.heading: A cosa serve
sections.text: jev-router avvia le CLI originali tramite un proxy locale e sceglie un livello di modello per ogni nuovo turno utente.

sections.heading: Ruolo di Jev
sections.text: Una chiamata Jev suggerisce il livello; le regole locali rispettano richieste esplicite, confidenza e dimensione della conversazione.

sections.heading: Come iniziare
sections.text: Installa con npm, configura JEV_API_KEY e avvia jev-claude o jev-codex con la CLI originale installata e autenticata.

sections.heading: Ambito e limiti
sections.text: Le continuazioni degli strumenti mantengono il livello iniziale; un errore Jev conserva il modello corrente. I file temporanei di spiegazione contengono prompt e scambio esatto di instradamento.
